instruction: I have a spreadsheet with research papers on my desktop. Find the oldest paper in the list by publication date and save its title to a text file named "oldest_paper.txt" in the /home/user directory.

metadata.explanation: Verified with Python: Oldest paper is 'Attention Is All You Need' published 2017/6/12. Evaluator checks if the text file contains this title.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the output file at /home/user/oldest_paper.txt and extracts text content
Metric correctly checks if the file contains the expected paper title 'Attention Is All You Need' using case-insensitive substring matching
Expected value is semantically correct - metadata confirms this is actually the oldest paper (published 2017/6/12)
The evaluator successfully verifies the main deliverable: the output file contains the correct title

Minor limitation: Evaluator only checks if the title appears in the file, but doesn't independently verify the agent correctly identified the oldest paper by re-analyzing the spreadsheet. However, this is pragmatic - if the correct title is present, the agent likely performed the task correctly
Substring matching could theoretically allow false positives (e.g., if file contains the title but states a different paper is oldest), but this edge case is unlikely in normal execution
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: For more robust verification, could add exact match check (e.g., file should contain ONLY the title, or title on its own line) to reduce false positive risk

Could optionally add a second verification step that re-reads the spreadsheet and confirms 'Attention Is All You Need' has the earliest publication date, but this adds significant complexity for marginal benefit
